ficha: Graphic design, design direction and consulting
Identity, web, 3D, fleet, campaigns, social media and sales material

parrafos: During our time leading design at GSP Seguridad, we handled the company's visual communication end to end, developing solutions for branding, advertising, corporate communication, social media and sales material.
The project included an identity update, a visual redesign of the website, a 3D logo animation, corporate pieces, fleet design and advertising campaigns for security, alarms and cameras.

On the commercial side we developed catalogs, brochures, presentations and manuals, turning technical information into clear, attractive and useful resources. We also created the visual line for social media, including the Instagram feed, story highlights and adaptations for LinkedIn and Facebook.
A more coherent, professional and competitive visual communication system, designed both for its aesthetics and for its commercial and communication purpose.

ficha: Latex paint, spray paint, roller and brush

bloques.destacado: Don David was going through a complete makeover: changes inside, a redefined commercial offer and a new name, Blend David. The mural was the last stage of that process and the first thing the public would see.
parrafos: The brief was to paint the entire façade —5.5 meters high by 8.5 meters wide, almost 47 m²— and bring to the street a transformation that until then only existed inside the store.

The starting point was the word that names the store: blend. From there came an abstract language built from fluid shapes, spills and organic masses that intertwine, like liquids in motion before they fully mix.

Deep black as the background, supporting the store's night-time presence and making the other colors pop. On top of it, magenta and violet, with yellow as an accent. Three colors on black: enough to make an impact from a distance without overloading the façade.

The mural is built around the sign: the shapes open and close around the logo, letting it breathe at the center. The piece continues under the awning and down to the ground-floor panels, so the whole façade reads as a single work.
Seven working days, coordinated with the reopening schedule. The result established the new name in the public space: today the façade is the brand's main identity asset.

equilibria.subtitulo: Brand identity and full digital presence
ficha: Identity, website, Google and Maps, contact channels and social media
Cloudflare Pages, on its own domain

bloques.destacado: Equilibria is a physical therapy practice in San Martín de los Andes, Argentina, that grew through word of mouth but had no website, no brand identity and no simple way to book an appointment. The goal was that when someone recommended it, the other person could easily find it, get to know it and get in touch.
It wasn’t just a website: we designed the whole patient journey, from searching for the practice to booking an appointment.
parrafos: Identity: a symbol of balancing stones, a navy and turquoise palette, and two typefaces used the same way across every channel.
Website: a single custom-built page with 13 sections, designed mobile-first, covering the practice, treatments, gym, home care, opening hours, FAQs and location.
Google and Maps: a set-up business profile with address, hours, website, phone, photos and posts, so anyone searching finds the right information.
Contact: 9 WhatsApp shortcuts with the message already written, automated messaging for first inquiries and email on its own domain.
Social media: Instagram with the same identity, six story highlights with custom icons and a series of posts presenting the space, the treatments and the way of working.

A complete, consistent system: the brand looks the same on Google, on the website and on Instagram, all the information is online, and every channel leads to booking in just a few steps. The website and Google also invite patients to leave their review.

parrafos: A story flyer gets two seconds of attention, with a thumb ready to swipe. That is why every piece layers the information: first the image that stops the scroll, then the party’s name, and only then date, line-up and venue.
The series for TKNO Radio and Intekno builds an identity you can recognize from one date to the next —logo, frames, grid and typefaces that repeat— while every edition changes its image and mood.
